definitions.explanation: An alternative name given to a person, place, or thing, often based on a notable characteristic. Unlike casual nicknames, {異名|いみょう} tends to be descriptive or literary in nature — more like a title or epithet.

examples.japanese: ⟦{京都|きょうと}→京都：09484_kyouto⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧「{千年|せんねん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{都|みやこ}→都：03747_miyako⟧」⟦という→という：09577_toiu⟧{異名|いみょう}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{知|し}られている→知る：00458_shiru⟧。
examples.english: Kyoto is known by the epithet 'the thousand-year capital.'

examples.japanese: ⟦その→その：00993_sono⟧⟦{武将|ぶしょう}→武将：13222_bushou⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{戦場|せんじょう}→戦場：12746_senjou⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{勇|いさ}ましさ⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧「⟦{虎|とら}→虎：02228_tora⟧」⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{異名|いみょう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{取|と}り→取る：00565_toru⟧、⟦{敵|てき}→敵：03546_teki⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{味方|みかた}→味方：03743_mikata⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{恐|おそ}れられていた→恐れる：02023_osoreru⟧。
examples.english: That military commander earned the epithet 'the tiger' for his bravery on the battlefield and was feared by both enemies and allies.

notes:
PRONUNCIATION:
Also read as いめい, but いみょう is more common in modern usage.

USAGE:
Often appears with ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{持|も}つ→持つ：00478_motsu⟧ (to have), ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{取|と}る→取る：00565_toru⟧ (to earn/take), or で⟦{知|し}られる→知る：00458_shiru⟧ (to be known by). Used for impressive or fearsome names rather than casual nicknames. Common in sports, historical, and literary contexts.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦あだ{名|な}→あだ名：10211_adana⟧: casual nickname — often playful
- {異名|いみょう}: epithet — more formal, descriptive, often impressive
- ⟦{通称|つうしょう}→通称：14404_tsuushou⟧: commonly known name — neutral, practical

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {異名|いみょう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{持|も}つ→持つ：00478_motsu⟧: have an epithet
- {異名|いみょう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{取|と}る→取る：00565_toru⟧: earn an epithet
- ～⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{異名|いみょう}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{呼|よ}ばれる→呼ぶ：00766_yobu⟧: be called by the epithet of ~
